```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", eval=FALSE)
```

scAgentKit provides a local browser interface and R functions for single-cell
RNA-seq analysis. You review the analysis plan, measured clustering and
cell-type annotations before retrieving a completed Seurat object. This guide
accompanies the package source from which it was built; use the matching
software environment when reopening an existing project.

## Try the browser workflow

Use SeuratObject's bundled PBMC dataset for a first run:

```{r browser, purl=FALSE}
library(scAgentKit)
data("pbmc_small", package = "SeuratObject")
example_dir <- tempfile("scagentkit-example-")
dir.create(example_dir)
input <- file.path(example_dir, "pbmc-small.rds")
saveRDS(pbmc_small, input)
project_dir <- file.path(example_dir, "project")

sc_start(input, project_dir,
  context = list(species = "human", tissue = "blood",
                 research_goal = "Explore the review workflow"),
  provider = "mock", doublet = "off")
```

This opens a local browser page. The mock provider needs no API key and sends
no data to an external model. Review the evidence at each step:

1. Inspect QC distributions and the analysis plan. Save any edits, then approve
   the reviewed plan to run the local analysis.
2. Inspect the measured clustering, marker contrasts and sample composition.
   Choose a resolution from the scan and approve the reviewed choice.
3. Inspect the annotation worksheet, markers and reference candidates. Complete
   each row with a label or Unknown, confidence, rationale and supporting
   markers. Save the complete proposal, inspect it, then approve annotation.

Saving a draft records edits without approving it. The small dataset and mock
responses demonstrate operation; they do not establish biological accuracy or
suitable parameters for a study.

## Retrieve and reopen results

After the browser reports completion:

```{r results, purl=FALSE}
result <- sc_result(project_dir)
table(result$sc_annotation)
sc_open(project_dir)$view$output
```

The project contains marker tables, figures, analysis settings and review
records. Preserve the complete project directory, original inputs and software
environment. A temporary directory is convenient for this trial; choose a
durable path for a study.

To reopen this example in the same environment:

```{r reopen, purl=FALSE}
sc_start(input, project_dir)
```

## Use your own data

Pass an RDS file containing counts or a Seurat object, a 10x MEX directory, or
a sample table to `sc_start()`. Supply verified species, tissue and sample
information. Declare sample, donor, capture and batch roles using the actual
metadata; unknown roles can remain unspecified. Inspect the import summary
before approving the analysis plan.

Model assistance is optional. Configure the selected provider and review the
aggregate data-transfer scope before requesting a suggestion. Scientific
approval is a separate decision. Function help describes the supported input
and configuration arguments:

```{r help, purl=FALSE}
help("sc_start", package = "scAgentKit")
help("sc_result", package = "scAgentKit")
```

## Complete scripted example

For a software installation check, the package also includes an offline
three-review tutorial:

```{r scripted, purl=FALSE}
source(system.file("examples", "three-gate-analysis.R",
                   package = "scAgentKit", mustWork = TRUE))
checked <- three_gate_analysis(tempfile("scagentkit-check-"))
checked$receipt
```

This script approves only its bundled public fixture, assigns Unknown labels
and checks completion and input preservation. Research data require your own
review at each decision. The interactive examples in this vignette are shown
without execution because they require browser interaction.
